items.e: AND THE LORD SPOKE. Scripture now mentions the first of the commandments given via Moses and Aaron, as they alone were prophets of the law. After them, except for extenuating circumstances as in the case of Gideon and Elijah, no new precepts were revealed. Do not take the chanting of psalms in the house of God instituted by David to heart, as the latter was an enactment and an institution established by David and Solomon. Thus Scripture states, by their beliefs (II Chron. 9:22), and not by their prophecies. However, Saadiah Gaon says that they had a tradition going back to Moses that a king would arise and innovate musical compositions. Neither carry forth a burden out of your houses on the sabbath day (Jer. 17:22) is similar.

THIS MONTH. Rabbi Judah Ha-Parsi says that the Israelites, like the uncircumcised, employed a solar calendar. He offers as proof, Thou shalt therefore keep this ordinance in its season (Ex. 13:10). But lunar years are not all equal, as the seasons of plowing and harvest are dependent solely on the movement of the sun as it travels to the north or the south. However, he did not speak correctly. I will now explain. We know that it takes the moon, moving in its sphere in a given point facing the sphere of the zodiac, close to twenty-seven and a third days to return to this very point. Now let us assume a starting point wherein the moon is in conjunction with the sun at the beginning of Aries. In such a case the moon would not find the sun at the head of Aries when it returned there because the sun, traveling in its mean motion, would by then have journeyed twenty-seven degrees. This is because, contrary to the movement above, the sun and the moon move from west to east. The sun and the moon would next be in conjunction at the end of twenty-nine and a half days, two-thirds and seventy-three parts of an hour, according to the way Israelites divide the hour. Thus the moon would have traveled the very degrees that the sun journeyed, and the moon also would have had to travel two days and close to five hours in the parts in which the sun had moved. Actually, the year belongs only to the sun, as the sun gives birth to the four seasons of the year, cold, heat, summer, and winter. Now let us assume the sun to be at the beginning of Aries. It will then travel three hundred and sixty-five days plus close to a quarter of a day in its sphere until it returns a second time to where it started out. It is for this reason that a year is called a shanah . Now the moon has no year, as the sun has no month. Nothing new happens to the sun; only to the light of the moon does something new occur. It is because of this that a month is called a chodesh and also a yerach . It is so called because the light of the moon is renewed. We have conclusive proof that the moon has no light of its own, and that its light comes from the sun. The sun therefore does not darken except in the moment when it is in conjunction with the moon at the head or the tail of Aries. Similarly, the moon does not darken except when it is opposite the sun in the aforementioned places at night. Due to the fact that the year of the uncircumcised is close to a solar year and because they saw that the moon is renewed twelve times during a solar year, they divided the days of the year into twelve parts and called each part a month because it is close to the days of a lunar month. This arrangement of theirs is not in keeping with the laws of nature. Similarly the Moslems, because their festivals are contingent upon lunar months and a month starts from the night that the moon is first seen. They saw that there are twelve months in a solar year and they did not find a closer way of reckoning than this, as there is only a difference of eleven days between the two ways of numbering the year. They therefore made all of their years lunar. The time of their Passover recedes each year by eleven days until thirty-three solar years equal thirty-four lunar years. These things are not based on the laws of nature. Now God commanded in His Torah that the festivals be kept in their seasons, for He said, Observe the month of spring and keep the passover unto the Lord thy God (Deut. 16:1). Now if spring is not found by half of the month then we make Passover in the month close to it. God similarly called the festival of Sha’vu’ot, the feast of harvest (Ex. 23:16) and the festival of Sukkot, the feast of ingathering ( Ibid .). The harvest and the ingathering are dependent on spring. Furthermore, we see that God said that we should not observe the Passover on any day but the midpoint of a lunar month. The same applies to the festival of Sukkot. God thus commanded that we observe lunar months and that the seasons of the festivals be preserved. Moses did not mention in the Torah that we should count twelve or thirteen months. He said only that we should begin the count in the month that we find spring. That month is to be called the first month whether the year has twelve or thirteen months. It is thus written, in the second month (Num. 10:11) and In the third month (Ex. 19:1). All the other months are similarly written. Nisan, Iyyar, Sivan, and all the other names of the months are not Hebrew. They are Chaldean terms. We therefore do not encounter these terms in any book of Scripture except in the Scroll of Esther and in the prophecies of Zechariah, Daniel, and Ezra, who were in the Diaspora. This then is its meaning: in the first month, which is called Nisan in the Chaldean tongue. However, we find three months called by other names in Hebrew, viz., in the month Ziv (I Kings 6:1); in the month Ethanim (I Kings 8:2); in the month Bul (I Kings 6:7). If we pursue the literal meaning of the text the month of Ziv is not Nisan but Iyyar, for it is written, in the month Ziv, which is the second month (I Kings 6:1), that is, which is known as the second to the first of the months of Israel. The words of Solomon’s reign ( Ibid .) are not connected to the word month but rather to the fourth year of Solomon’s reign ( Ibid. ), as we do not find the months related in the account of any king. Scripture only reports the year that the king started his reign. In the second day of the second month, in the fourth year of his reign recorded in Chronicles (II Chron. 3:2) is proof of this. We can refute Judah Ha-Parsi with the argument that not all years are equal. The years differ, due to the effect of the planets, in that the rain increases or diminishes and the heat or cold increases or diminishes each month, making it different from the known norm. Spring is therefore not be found to have arrived when the sun returns to the spot that it was in at the beginning of the previous year although it was then spring. There is more than a year and two weeks between one spring and the next. The Israelites therefore relied on the spring found in their country in whatever month it occurred, as the time of the appearance of spring varies in all countries according to the distance of that land from the equator. I will now give you a general rule. Although the Israelites in the time of the Holy Temple watched for the arrival of spring, the establishment of a leap year was not in their hands. It rather depended on the Bet Din which, as is related in the Mishnah, looked for other things besides spring. Now Moses did not explain to us in the Torah how we should establish years or months. Neither did he tell us what we should do if we do not find it to be spring. One can pose a difficult question from all this, namely, why did Moses explain the laws of the plagues of the leper, which fall upon one person and do not last forever, and leave out of the Torah the laws of the festivals that all of Israel is obligated to keep at all times? Furthermore, eating leaven on Passover and eating on the Day of Atonement are punished with excision. If Moses relied on the conjunction of the moon and sun he should have explained whether he meant according to the moon’s mean motion or its true conjunction, which takes place opposite the sphere of the constellations, because at times there are approximately fourteen hours between the calculated conjunction and the true conjunction. It is because of this that our holy fathers said, “At times it comes at longer intervals; at times it comes at shorter intervals.” Only one who knows his way in the science of astronomy can know this. Additionally, Moses should have explained from which part of the earth we reckon the conjunction. For behold, between Jerusalem and this city, whose name is Lucca, there is more than three hours. If Moses relied on the time the moon is first seen he should have explained the place of its sighting, as the Arc of Vision changes in each place according to the earth’s latitude and according to the latitude of the moon from the line of the constellations, in addition to changes in visibility due to longitude, latitude, atmospheric conditions, and the height of elevation or lack thereof. All of these things require lengthy exposition. Now if it is cloudy, shall we out of doubt observe the new moon for two days? This proves that the establishment of the new moon is contingent on the declaration of the Bet Din in each generation. They had a tradition that the Bet Din establish seven leap years every nineteen years, totaling two hundred and thirty-five months or six thousand, nine hundred and thirty-nine and two-thirds days, plus five hundred and ninety-five parts of an hour. The aforementioned are nineteen solar years without addition or subtraction. Do not concern yourself with the hour and four hundred and eighty-five parts of an hour according to “Samuel’s calendar.” We know that this was not hidden from him. Samuel only used a number which was close in his time to the men of his generation. Today there is a difference of close to nine days between the true circuit and Samuel’s circuit. Do not be amazed at this. For behold the Braita states that one who wants to know the place of the moon should calculate the year of the world and divide it into months and divide the months into twenty-nine and a half days and two-thirds of an hour, i.e., seven hundred and twenty parts of an hour. Now seventy-three parts are missing. They will add up to more than two-thirds of a day each cycle. There will thus be a difference of close to half a year between the calculation of the conjunctions from creation and our own calculation of the conjunction. It has thus been made clear to you that the sum of our years equals out every cycle of solar years, and our months are always lunar months. Blessed be the Lord who has guided me in the straight path. I will now offer you proof from Scripture that the festivals are dependent upon the Bet Din. Scripture states, For the king had taken counsel, and his princes, and all the congregation in Jerusalem, to keep the passover in the second month (II Chron. 30:2). Now if they had a tradition to look for spring, as those who argue with our rabbis of blessed memory claim, why did the king take counsel to establish the Passover in the second month? It will now be shown if their words are true. Hezekiah did three evils. First of all, he did not offer the Passover sacrifice in its time although he was ritually clean. Why did Hezekiah delay the observance of Passover because most of the congregation had not arrived? Such a thing is only found in the words of tradition, not in Scripture. Second, he ate and caused Israel to eat leaven in the first month. Third, on his own he decided to observe the festival of unleavened bread in the second month. Such a thing is not to be done. With the exception of eating the paschal lamb on one night, the Lord did not command the observance of the Passover in the second month, for all those who are unclean eat unleavened bread along with all of Israel in the first month. Far be it for Hezekiah to do such evil. Moreover, Scripture says of him that he did not turn aside to the right or left from the commandments of the Lord. Furthermore, Hezekiah himself said in his prayer, Remember now, O Lord, I beseech Thee, how I have walked before Thee…and have done that which is good in Thy sight (II Kings 20:3). I will now explain. Know that Hezekiah took counsel with the entire congregation at the start of the first month that they should observe the Passover in the following month because most of the people had not arrived and the priests had not sanctified themselves in sufficient numbers. He thus added a month to the year, and the Passover that he observed was the actual Passover in its proper season. The fact that God plagued those who ate the paschal lamb in a manner contrary to what is written is proof of this. If the Passover observed by Hezekiah was not celebrated in its proper time and was therefore not acceptable to the Lord, why did He plague them? If Hezekiah sinned how is it that he prayed on their behalf and the Lord accepted his supplication and healed the people? The answer to one who would argue that the sages of blessed memory did not maintain that Hezekiah acted properly in adding another month during the month of Nisan is: they spoke the truth. It is the custom of every Bet Din to ascertain at the end of the month of Adar whether it is necessary to add another month to the year or not. Now Hezekiah did not do this; he committed a small error in adding another month to the year at the beginning of the month. Now since the additional month always comes before the first month, the latter is always the first of the months, and the festivals will fall in the seventh month from it. This is the meaning of it shall be the first month of the year to you (v. 2). We know that many commandments are in memory of the Exodus from Egypt. Behold, it is therefore fitting that the Exodus be the first reference point in Israel’s calculations. Thus it is written, And it came to pass in the four hundred and eightieth year after the children of Israel were come out of the land of Egypt, in the fourth year…in the month Ziv, which is the second month (I Kings 6:1). The gentiles ask, if the year is made up of months and the month of spring is its foundation and beginning, why do you calculate your years from the seventh month and say that a new year begins on its first day? The answer is that our sages of blessed memory have already noted that there are four new year days. We clearly see that the sanctification of the jubilee year is on the tenth day of the seventh month (Lev. 25:9). Furthermore, God commanded that the Torah be read in the set time of the year of release, in the feast of tabernacles (Deut. 31:10)… that they may hear, and that they may learn (Deut. 31:12). Now if the beginning of the year of release is reckoned from Nisan, why didn’t God command that the Torah be read during the festival of unleavened bread? Now they were idle for half a year. Furthermore, Scripture states, and the feast of ingathering at the turn of the year (Ex. 34:22). Elsewhere it states, at the end of the year , when thou gatherest in thy labors out of the field (Ex. 23:16). Additionally, we can derive the aforementioned from the way the Torah speaks and from the way nature acts. The Torah first states, ye shall not sow and afterwards says, neither (shall ye) reap (Lev. 25:12). The season of sowing is close to Tishri, not Nisan. Furthermore, if we reckon the beginning of the year of release from Nisan he who sowed in the sixth year will not harvest in the seventh year, because the harvest falls after Nisan when the year of release has already started. He will also not sow in the year of release. We thus see that the words of our sages are correct.

THE BEGINNING OF MONTHS. Rabbi Moses Ha-Kohen says that there is no need to use the term rosh chodesh (new moon). The term chodesh suffices, since the meaning of chodesh is the day that the light of the moon is renewed. Scripture thus states, chodesh ve-shabbat (New moon and sabbath) (Is. 1:13); chodshekhem u-mo’adekhem (your new moons and your appointed seasons) (Is. 1:14); mi-de chodesh be-chodsho (from one new moon to another) (Is. 66:23). Others argued with him and asked, if this be the case, then why does Scripture state, ba-chodesh hashe’vi’i be-echad la-chodesh (And in the seventh month, on the first day of the month) (Num. 29:1)? Rabbi Moses Ha-Kohen answered, to remove doubt. They also quoted, u-ve-roshe chodshekhem (and in your new moons) (Num. 28:11) against him. He answered that Scripture speaks of the month of Nisan throughout the years, for only Nisan is the chief new moon. They then asked him, if so, then what sacrifices are we to offer on other new moons? He answered that Scripture states in the very same portion, This is the burnt-offering of every new moon throughout the months of the year (Num. 28:14). Scripture likewise states, Also in the day of your gladness, and in your appointed seasons, and in your new moons (u-ve-roshe chodshekhem), ye shall blow with the trumpets (Num. 10:10) because it is the beginning of the year. However, we will not set aside the words of our rabbis of blessed memory because of our own opinions. Our sages said that we sound the trumpets on the new moon of every month. It is correct to say chodesh or rosh chodesh . It is written, ad chodesh yamim (but a whole month) (Num. 11:20), the meaning of which is: until the days of the month are complete.
SPEAK YE UNTO ALL THE CONGREGATION OF THE CHILDREN OF ISRAEL. For all those who are obligated to observe the commandments are required to do this.

THEY SHALL TAKE. Whoever has cattle shall take from his cattle, as the Israelites had a lot of cattle. Or yikchu (they shall take) means they shall buy. Yefet says that they should start preparing the lamb on the tenth day and do so till the fourteenth day. However, we do not know whether this is a command for all generations or pertained only to the Passover observed in Egypt.
A LAMB, ACCORDING TO THEIR FATHERS’ HOUSES. If they be few.

A LAMB FOR A HOUSEHOLD. If they be many. After stating, a lamb, according to their fathers’ houses , Scripture says a lamb for each and every household. I have already explained the meaning of bayit (household) at the beginning of this book.
AND IF THE HOUSEHOLD BE TOO LITTLE FOR A LAMB. Too little to eat a lamb because the members of the household are few. Then he and his neighbor shall take a lamb.

ACCORDING TO THE NUMBER OF THE SOULS. Mikhsat (number of) means a portion. The word mekhes (tribute) in And the Lord’s tribute (Num. 31:37) in which mekhes refers to the portion which each one shall take, is similar. So too the word kosi (portion) in O Lord, the share of mine inheritance and my portion (Ps. 16:5). This is also the meaning of takhosu (ye shall make your count). It comes from a double root. The doubled letter is missing in the word be-mikhsat and also in mekhes . Scripture follows the paradigm of memer (bitterness) in And bitterness to her that bore him (Prov. 17:25), which comes from a double root in its vocalization of mekhes .

YOUR LAMB SHALL BE WITHOUT BLEMISH. It shall be without any deformity. The word seh (lamb) also applies to the two kinds taken in by the term tzon (flock). Sehkhevasim ve-seh izzim (the sheep and the goat) (Deut. 14:4) is similar. Rabbi Moses ben Amram Ha-Parsi says that the obligation to offer a lamb only pertains to the Passover brought in Egypt. However, in the Land of Israel one could sacrifice a lamb or a bull. He offers as proof, And thou shalt sacrifice the passover-offering unto the Lord thy God, of the flock and the herd (Deut. 16:2), which applies to the Passover to be offered in all future generations. However, he did not speak correctly. All future Passover offerings are in memory of the paschal lamb offered in Egypt, and one should not deviate from it. The meaning of the aforementioned verse can only be: And thou shalt sacrifice the passover-offering unto the Lord thy God of the flock as an obligation; and of the herd , bring peace offerings to be eaten cooked in water. Similarly, And thou shalt rejoice in thy feast, thou, and thy son, and thy daughter (Deut. 16:14) means thou art obligated; thy son and thy daughter are permitted to do so. Proof of the above is found in the book of Chronicles. We read there that on the fourteenth day they slaughtered lambs and bullocks. It is written there that the lambs were for Passover offerings and the bullocks which served as peace offerings were cooked in pots and caldrons. Only those sacrifices which came from the flock were roasted in the fire according to ordinance. Rabbi Joshua says that there is a difference between ben shanah (of the first year) and ben shenato (of the first year). A ben shanah has lived a year and ben shenato means exactly what Scripture says. Now with regard to the sacrifices offered by the princes it first states, keves echad ben shenato leolah (one he-lamb of the first year, for a burnt-offering) (Num. 7:15) and then states, kevasim bene shanah (he-lambs of the first year) (Num. 7:87).
AND YE SHALL KEEP IT. Each one shall keep it in his house.

AT DUSK. Ben ha-arbayim (at dusk) is a difficult phrase. Rabbi Solomon says that it refers to the moment after midday that the sun moves to the west. He does not explain why arbayim is in the dual form. Now, Scripture states, And when Aaron lighteth the lamps at dusk (ben ha-arbayim) (Ex. 30:8), and there is no doubt that Aaron is to light the lamps when the sun sets. Now, when we researched this phrase we found that Scripture refers to the moment of ben ha-arbayim as erev (evening). For it is clearly written, At dusk (ben ha-arbayim) ye shall eat flesh (Ex. 16:12), and it is there stated, when the Lord shall give you in the evening (ba-erev) flesh to eat (Ex. 16:8). Likewise, concerning the lighting of the lamps it is written: Aaron and his sons shall set it in order, to burn from evening (erev) to morning before the Lord (Ex. 27:21). It is similarly written, even burnt-offerings mornings and evening (erev) (Ezra 3:3), and it is stated, The one lamb thou shalt offer in the morning; and the other lamb thou shalt offer at dusk (ben ha-arbayim) (Ex. 29:39). Now concerning the Passover sacrifice, about which the term ben ha-arbayim (at dusk) is employed, we find that Scripture states, there thou shalt sacrifice the passover-offering at even (erev), at the coming (bo) of the sun, at the season that thou earnest forth out of Egypt (Deut. 16:6). Rabbi Solomon explains that the reference is to the time that the sun comes to the west. However, this is not the meaning of bo . It refers to the opposite of the sun’s going forth upon the earth since it is written, the sun went out (yatza) upon the earth (Gen. 19:23), which means the time that the sun first begins to be seen on the earth. Similarly, And when the sun comes (ba) he shall be clean (Lev. 22:7) means when the sun shall no longer be seen upon the ground. Now it is written concerning a nocturnal seminal emission, But it shall be, when evening cometh on, he shall bathe himself in water; and when the sun comes (u-khe-vo ha-shemesh) he may come within the camp (Deut. 23:12). If this is not so, then let Rabbi Solomon explain what difference there is between “when the sun comes” with regard to Passover and “when the sun comes” with regard to a nocturnal seminal emission. It is the same with and when the sun comes he shall be clean (Lev. 22:7). The Sadducees say that there are three evenings. Their proof is from a verse which they found to read, ha-erev ha-shelishit (the third evening) (I Sam. 20:5). However, they do not recognize or understand the truth. It is written, Tomorrow is the new moon…And in the third day thou shalt hide thyself well (I Sam. 20:18, 19), the meaning of which is: when close to evening of the third day starting from today comes, you shall hide yourself well in the field where you are presently hidden. It is because of this that Jonathan said, until the third evening . I will now backtrack and explain. Know that the word arbayim is always vocalized according to the paradigm of the dual forms like ovnayim (birthstool) (Ex. 1:16). Luchotayim (planks) (Ezek. 27:5) is similar. So is derachayim (ways) (Prov. 28:18), as But he that is perverse in his ways (derachayim) shall fall in one of them ( Ibid. ) proves. The same is the case with the word shamayim (heaven), as the heavens consist of two poles which are like fastened nails upon which the sphere leans. I have already explained in The Book of God , the Glorious, that the word shamayim comes from the same root as the word sham (there) in There the upright might reason with Him (Job 23:7). The term shamayim alludes to these two places. We thus have two evenings: one when the sun sets, that is, the time when the sun descends beneath the earth; the second when its light disappears from the clouds. Now there is close to one and a third hours between them. It is at this time that one who experienced a seminal emission may enter the camp and Aaron kindles the lights. Rabbi Saadiah Gaon, of blessed memory, says that the altar of the burnt offering measured five cubits in length and five cubits in width. Such an area has room only for a small number of kohanim (priests), who are the ones that sprinkle the blood from the paschal lambs before it coagulates. Now in the days of Josiah, when the number of Israelites were few, the kohanim were not able to sprinkle the blood of the Passover offerings and the peace offerings that they slaughtered; i.e., they were not able to sprinkle them on the altar in one and a third hours. How much more unable to do so were they when all the tribes were in their country. There was thus a tradition that they begin to slaughter from the moment that it became clear to a person that the sun turned to the west. Scripture speaks of ben ha-arbayim (at dusk) because most of the paschal lambs were slaughtered then, and that marks its time limit; for one should not wait until the going down of the sun’s light.
ON THE TWO SIDE-POSTS. Of the door of the house. Moses will go on to explain how they are to take the blood.

[LINTEL.] The word mashkof (lintel) means a window. Compare, va-yashkef (looked) (Gen. 26:8). This window was in the door. This is the custom in all Moslem countries. The practice of the uncircumcised differs from that of the Egyptians even regarding food, an example being, Thou shalt break it in pieces (Lev. 2:6). Similarly with regard to women’s jewelry such as the wearing of nose rings and earrings and all that the prophet Isaiah mentioned concerning the daughters of Zion (Is. 3:18-24). Likewise, all of their houses without exception are built in courtyards. One entrance is called the door to the house and the other the gate of the courtyard. Many say that the purpose of placing the blood on the window and on the two side-posts was to demonstrate publicly that they slaughtered the abomination of Egypt, since by then the fear of the Israelites had fallen on the Egyptians, and the Israelites were not afraid of being stoned. Now if this was the case then the blood should have been placed on the entrance to the courtyard. However, the blood was placed in secret, for they closed the gate of the courtyard. Furthermore, they slaughtered the lamb at dusk, which is close to night, so that no one would see them. Moreover, no man left his house until the morning when each one went on his way and each one closed the gate to his courtyard. The Egyptians thought that the Israelites would return. The reason the blood was smeared on the window was to make atonement for all those eating in the house and to serve as a mark for the destroyer to see. It is to be understood in the same way as and set a mark on the foreheads of the men (Ezek. 9:4).

[HOUSES.] The word battim (houses) is grammatically irregular, as it has a dagesh following a long kamatz . This is contrary to the rule whereby a dagesh is only placed after a short kamatz , as in ronnu (sing) in Sing, O ye heavens (Is. 44:23). Perhaps battim was vocalized with a kamatz because of the missing yod in the word bayit . This form would thus not be confused with the form battim (baths) in ten baths are a homer (Ezek. 45:14) wherein battim , the plural of bat (bath) in The ephah and the bath (Ezek. 45:11), is vocalized with a pattach in the plural. The word battim (houses) in upon the houses is indicative, for unlike the rule it is penultimately accented.

WITH BITTER HERBS THEY SHALL EAT IT. One of the Spanish wise men explained that it is well known that because of the Nile and the lack of rain, the humidity in Egypt is very high and the air is always moist. It was therefore their custom to eat all sorts of bitter herbs and mustards with their meals. An Egyptian always had bitters in which to dip his bread, even if he had but one loaf of bread, because the bitters are a cure for their climate. However, we will rely on the opinion of our ancients of blessed memory, who explained to us that the reason for the bitter herbs is to remind us that they made their lives bitter (Ex. 1:14).

RAW. Some say that the meaning of na (raw) is: as it is now, i.e., when the meat is raw. However, we do not find the word na used in such a way elsewhere in Scripture. Others say that it comes from the same root as heni (breaks) in But if her father breaks her vow (Num. 30:6) and means broken. However, this is incorrect, as Scripture later states, neither shall ye break a bone thereof (v. 46). However, in my opinion the word na has no counterpart in Scripture. It means the opposite of cooked and is referred to as chai (raw). Compare, For he will not have sodden flesh of thee, but raw (chai) (I Sam. 2:15). I have previously noted that most of Arabic is similar to Hebrew. Now in Arabic raw meat is called nayy , and the alef heh, vav , and yod interchange in the tongue of the Arabs as it does in our tongue.

NOR SODDEN. Bashel (sodden) is an adjective. Here its meaning is, that which is sodden with water. That which is roasted in fire is also called mevushal , for it is written, And thou shalt roast (u-vishalta) and eat it (Deut. 16:7) and, And they roasted (va-yevashelu) the passover with fire according to the ordinance (II Chron. 35:13). It is possible that nor sodden at all with water means nor cooked, that is, cooked in water, as a royal dish is sodden in liquids. They place a wide copper utensil on the fire and fill half of it with water. When the water boils they place the pot with the meat in cold water above the boiling water. Thus is the meat cooked. This dish is better than one prepared close to the fire. I the writer add to the words of this scholar what I heard from his very own mouth. Bashel (sodden) is an adjective following the paradigm of kaved (heavy) and zaken (old). The term bashel here is similar, as its bet is vocalized with a kamatz and its shin has no dagesh. Bashel is not an infinitive like kabbed (promote) in for I will promote thee (Num. 22:17) or hakkeh (smite) in thou shalt surely smite (Deut. 13:16), as the infinitive is not joined to a word unless it is a perfect or an imperfect. Compare, dabber yedabber (speak well) (Ex. 4:14), and hakdesh hikdashti (I verily dedicate) (Jud. 17:3). However, the infinitive is never joined with the po’el or pa’ul . Thus bashel (sodden) is similar to kaved (heavy). Its feminine form is beshelah , as in the shoulder…when it is sodden (beshelah) (Num. 6:19). Do not ask what need Scripture had to use the two terms bashel and mevushal . As the scholar pointed out, there are two soddenings, one of which is the placing of the utensil with the meat in the midst of the boiling water. The plural of bashel mevushal is beshelim mevushalim . Compare, chakhamim mechukkamim (exceeding wise) in But they are exceeding wise (Prov. 30:24). The singular form is chakham mechukkam . Compare, barukh u-mevorakh (exceedingly blessed). There is a difference in nuance from a grammatical standpoint between chakham (a wise man) and mechukkam (one who has become wise). There is, as the scholar explained, a similar difference between bashel (sodden) and mevushal (sodden).

ITS HEAD WITH ITS LEGS AND WITH THE INWARDS THEREOF. The word al has the meaning of with. The word al in And they came, both men and (al) women (Ex. 35:22) is similar. The head and the legs are to be washed in water as the ordinance requires.

BUT THAT WHICH REMAINETH OF IT…BURN WITH FIRE. If one was unable to eat one’s portion due to circumstances beyond one’s control. Yefet says that the reference is to the bones. However, Scripture only speaks of what is normal.

AND THUS SHALL YE EAT IT. The reference is only to the paschal lamb eaten in Egypt. However, those in Argalon do the same today in memory of the Exodus. These spiritual errants all leave their land on the fifteenth day in memory of the Exodus.
AND YOUR STAFF IN YOUR HAND. To lead the asses. Compare, and he smote the ass with his staff (Num. 22:27).

[IN HASTE.] Israel was not to delay. They were to hurry and eat the paschal lamb before the moment of destruction arrived, when God would pass over their homes. God therefore commanded that the lamb be roasted in fire, because food that is roasted cooks quickly. The holy patriarchs similarly said the paschal lamb may be eaten only until midnight and it may only be eaten roasted.
FOR I WILL GO THROUGH THE LAND OF EGYPT. God’s might and His power passed throughout the land. Hence it was as if God Himself went throughout the land.

AND AGAINST ALL THE GODS OF EGYPT I WILL EXECUTE JUDGMENTS. In the manner of Dagon was fallen upon his face to the ground (I Sam. 5:4). It is similarly written, upon their gods also the Lord executed judgments (Num. 33:4).

AND THE BLOOD SHALL BE TO YOU FOR A TOKEN. This shall be for you a token so that your hearts will be strong and will not weaken as you hear the cries of the Egyptians when their first-born die via the destroyer. [AND WHEN I SEE THE BLOOD.] I will pass over you and there will be no plague among you because I will see the blood. The blood will be a sign to the destroyer.
AND THIS DAY SHALL BE UNTO YOU. It shall be a memorial for generations.

AND YE SHALL KEEP IT A FEAST. The reference is to the feast of Passover. Scripture says that it shall be kept a feast by an ordinance throughout your generations. However, it does not say that it is to be kept in all of your dwelling places, because this commandment is, as I will explain, contingent on dwelling in the Land of Israel.

SEVEN DAYS SHALL YE EAT UNLEAVENED BREAD. The reason for shall ye eat unleavened bread is to recall the matzot eaten when they left Egypt. They were not previously commanded to eat unleavened bread save for that which is to be eaten with the paschal lamb before midnight. However, God now commanded that they eat unleavened bread for seven days in memory of what happened to them when they left Egypt, as it is written there, for it was not leavened (Ex. 12:39). Had the Egyptians permitted them to tarry a bit, they would have leavened their dough. They ate unleavened bread for seven days until Pharaoh was drowned on the seventh day. The heavenly cloud led them day and night and they did not tarry very long even when they camped. It is similarly written when discussing the paschal lamb, seven days shalt thou eat unleavened bread therewith, even the bread of affliction (Deut. 16:3). Now according to its plain meaning, the text Seven days shall ye eat unleavened bread is stating an obligation. That thou mayest remember the day when thou camest forth out of the land of Egypt all the days of thy life (Deut. 16:3) is proof of this. It is because of this that Scripture states, Ye shall eat nothing leavened; in all your habitations shall ye eat unleavened bread (Ex. 12:20), as the latter is an obligation within the Land of Israel and outside of the Land of Israel.

[HOWBEIT THE FIRST DAY YE SHALL PUT AWAY LEAVEN OUT OF YOUR HOUSES.] Now since Israel had a tradition of commencing the slaughter of the paschal lamb when the sun started going down towards the west, and it is written, Thou shalt not offer the blood of My sacrifice with leavened bread (Ex. 34:25), the rabbis of blessed memory interpreted the word ach (howbeit) to mean a part of. Mark the fact that ceasing an act is not an act. The meaning of And on the seventh day God finished (Gen. 2:2) is: when the seventh day started God had already finished his work. Similarly, the meaning of the first day ye shall put away leaven out of your houses is: when the first day starts, all leaven shall already have been removed from the houses. Now the first day starts at the end of the fourteenth day at even, as it is written, from the first day until the seventh day . The meaning of the phrase then is that the seven full days are from the fourteenth day of the month at even, which is the end of the fourteenth day, until the twenty-first day at even. I will yet speak concerning this.
AND IN THE FIRST DAY. The day of the Exodus from Egypt. The seventh day is, as I will explain, the day that the Egyptians drowned.

NO MANNER OF WORK. We do not find the phrase kol melakhah (no manner of work) stated with regard to any of the festivals, with the exception of the Sabbath and the Day of Atonement. However, the phrase is employed with regard to Passover with the proviso that that which every man must eat is permitted. In all other places, be it Passover, Sha’vu’ot, the Day of Memorial, or the festival of Sukkot, Scripture employs the abridged form and states, ye shall do no manner of servile work . Only in one place with regard to Passover is it stated that you shall do no manner of work under the first stated conditions.
AND YE SHALL OBSERVE. God here commanded that the matzot be watched from the time of the harvest.

[HAVE I BROUGHT.] Scripture reads, have I brought your hosts out of the land of Egypt although they had not yet left Egypt. This prophecy took place at the beginning of the month. It meaning is: you will say this in all of your generations.

IN THE FIRST. Scripture uses an abridged form since it had already stated, it shall be the first month of the year to you (v. 2). The meaning of in the first thus is, in the first month. In the tenth, on the first day of the month (Gen. 8:5) is similar.

LEAVEN. Se’or (leaven) refers to something which induces leavening. The substance is well known. Scripture then goes on to say, for whosoever eateth anything which is leavened (machmetzet). Note that from the first day until the seventh day (v. 15) is not connected to what is adjacent, i.e., to shall be cut off but rather is connected to for whosoever eateth leavened bread . It is similar to of Solomon’s reign over Israel (I Kings 6:1). Yefet says that some letters refer both to the word in which they are placed and to a word previously written, as in odem pitdah u-vareket (carnelian, topaz, and smaragd) (Ex. 28:17), which is to be interpreted as if written, odem u-pitdah u-vareket (carnelian, and topaz, and smaragd). The same is true of mi-yom ha-rishon ad yom ha-shevi’i (from the first day until the seventh day).

[WHETHER HE BE A SOJOURNER.] Scripture already noted that whosoever eateth leavened bread from among the Israelites incurs the penalty of excision. Scripture now adds a sojourner who is a sincere proselyte.

NOTHING LEAVENED. Scripture first mentions the punishment and then the warning. In all your habitations shall ye eat unleavened bread is not optional as Six days shall work be done (Ex. 35:2) is. On the contrary, it is an obligation so that one will remember.
AND MOSES CALLED FOR ALL THE ELDERS OF ISRAEL. So that they would tell the people.
AND TAKE YOU LAMBS. On the tenth day, as he was commanded by God.

[AND KILL THE PASSOVER LAMB.] The grammarian says that ve-shachatu (and kill) in and kill the passover lamb is a pi’el . However, he spoke incorrectly. Ve-shachatu (shall kill it) in and the whole congregation of Israel shall kill it (v. 6) is a kal . It is properly vocalized with a kamatz beneath the shin because of the silent missing letter. However, ve-shachatu (and kill) in and kill the passover lamb is imperative in the kal . We do not find this root in the pi’el in any place in Scripture. The shin of ve-shachatu should have been vocalized with a chirik , as miskhu (draw) is. However, since the shin is followed by a guttural it was vocalized with a pattach , as is Hebrew practice. Compare, bacharu (choose) in choose you (Josh. 24:15). There are many other similar instances. The shin is therefore vocalized with a long pattach in the imperative. Both words are from the same conjugation.
AND YE SHALL TAKE. Moses now explains the manner in which the blood is to be taken and placed on the lintel.

[A BUNCH OF.] The word aguddat means a bunch (of). Compare, la-aggudah (band) in and became one band (II Sam. 2:25). Rabbi Merinus says that the alef in aguddah is appended, as aguddah comes from the same root as gedud (troop). Others say that the alef in aguddah is a root letter like the alef in afuddato (skillfully woven) in and the skillfully woven band (Ex 28:6).

[HYSSOP.] Rabbi Saadiah Gaon says that azov (hyssop) is a plant known in Arabic as zatr and in the vernacular as oregano. It is an herb distinguished by various kinds of flavors. However, this interpretation is incorrect, for Scripture states, even unto the hyssop that springeth out of the wall (I Kings 5:13). I do not know the identity of the azov . However, logically speaking it is not a very mighty plant for it is the opposite of the cedar mentioned in Scripture.

[BASIN.] Some say that they slaughtered the paschal lamb in the threshold of the gate, and they dipped the hyssop into it and then touched the side-posts with the blood. They say that the word saf (basin) is similar in meaning to the word saf (threshold) in and he measured the threshold (saf) of the gate (Ezek. 40:6) and to sippim (thresholds) in and the posts of the thresholds moved (Is. 6:4). Others say that saf (basin) is similar to sappot (basins) in brought beds, and basins (II Sam. 17:28) and that saf is a vessel over which they slaughtered the paschal lamb.
[UNTIL THE MORNING.] I will yet explain what this means.

AND WILL NOT SUFFER. He will not suffer the destroyer. Yitten (will suffer) here is similar in meaning to netatikha (suffered I thee) in Therefore suffered I thee not (Gen. 20:6). Now, the destroyer is under God’s power. If God allows him to come into their homes it is as if He gave him permission to do so.

AND YE SHALL OBSERVE THIS THING. Many are of the opinion that the placing of the blood on the lintel and on the two side-posts is an obligation for all generations because this thing is connected to the taking of the hyssop and dipping it into the lamb’s blood. Furthermore, Scripture afterwards states, for that he passed over the houses of the children of Israel in Egypt (v. 27). This interpretation would be correct from a logical point of view were it not for the true tradition which states otherwise. The correct interpretation is that this thing refers to and kill the passover lamb . The meaning of the children’s question is, when your children will see their family in a group eating an entire lamb, whose bones one is prohibited to break, with its head, with its legs, and with the inwards thereof, unlike the custom on all other festivals, and from which a gentile, an uncircumcised one, a sojourner, and a hired servant may not eat, they will question you.

AND IT SHALL COME TO PASS. Moses now explains that the slaughter of the paschal lamb is contingent upon dwelling in the Land of Israel. Do not be troubled by the Passover observed by Israelites at Mount Sinai. That was a commandment from on high. They did not observe another Passover in the desert. At Mount Sinai they were in an inhabited land and were thus able to find unleavened bread. However, when they were in a land that no man passed through they only had manna.
AND IT SHALL COME TO PASS…WHAT MEAN YE BY THIS SERVICE. The strange ritual that I noted.

THAT YE SHALL SAY: IT IS THE SACRIFICE OF THE LORD’S PASSOVER. The word pesach (passover) is to be rendered pity, as we find, paso’ach ve-himlit (He will pity it and He will rescue it) (Is. 31:5). The lamb is termed pesach (passover), as in and kill the passover (pesach) (v. 21), because God had pity on the first-born of Israel because of the blood of the lamb. However, Rabbi Saadiah Gaon says that the word pesach is derived from the word pi’se’ach (limp), since a lame person supports himself on his healthy leg. The destroyer acted in a similar manner. He exterminated the first-born in the Egyptian home and passed over the home of his Hebrew neighbor and did not destroy him. The term posechim (hopping) in How long will you keep hopping between two opinions (I Kings 18:20) is similar.
AND THE CHILDREN OF ISRAEL WENT AND DID SO. They took a lamb on the tenth day of the month. They did as the Lord had commanded Moses and Aaron: This is the ordinance of the passover (v. 43).
AND IT CAME TO PASS AT MIDNIGHT. The reference is to the second half of the night.

[UNTO THE FIRST-BORN OF THE CAPTIVE THAT WAS IN THE DUNGEON.] Yefet says that the captives who grind the millstone in prison during the day are put at night into a pit whose opening is covered with the millstone. This is the meaning of behind the mill (Ex. 11:5).
AND PHARAOH ROSE UP. He himself. But the Levites alone shall do the service (Num. 18:23), meaning the Levite himself, is similar.
FOR THERE WAS NOT A HOUSE WHERE THERE WAS NOT ONE DEAD. Scripture speaks of the majority of houses.

AND HE CALLED. Logically speaking Moses and Aaron were not in the land of Rameses with the Israelites on the night of the fifteenth. On the contrary, they were in that part of Egypt in which was the royal seat where Pharaoh lived. Now Moses and Aaron left the doors of their homes at midnight in accordance with God’s dictate. After Pharaoh gave the Israelites permission to go and worship God, Moses went with the servants of Pharaoh to Rameses to bring Israel out of Egypt. It is common knowledge in our time that there are six Persian miles between ancient Egypt, where Joseph’s treasures are known to be until this very day, and Rameses. Now the Israelites began to leave Egypt in the morning, namely, at the break of dawn when the light of the sun is seen in the clouds. There is a full hour and a third between the moment that dawn breaks and sunrise. We find that it can be very dark and still be morning. Thus Scripture states, And she lay down at his feet till the morning (Ruth 3:14), and then adds, before one could discern another . Now some Israelites exited Egypt at the break of dawn when, from the Torah’s standpoint, it is still night until sunrise. This group was close to Egypt. Another group who were further from Egypt exited that very day. The Israelites constituted a very large congregation. It is more than eight Persian miles from one end of Rameses to another. Scripture therefore states in one place, the Lord thy God brought thee forth out of Egypt by night (Deut. 16:1), and elsewhere reads, This day ye go forth (Ex. 13:4). It is further stated, the children of Israel went out with a high hand in the sight of all the Egyptians (Num. 33:3), and it is there recorded, while the Egyptians were burying them that the Lord had smitten . Now the Egyptians buried their dead during the day. I have thus explained the meaning of morning.
BOTH YE…AS YE HAVE SAID. Our cattle also shall go with us (Ex. 10:26).
[AND BLESS ME ALSO.] Pharaoh asked them to bless him and pray for him.
[ALSO.] Scripture reads also because Pharaoh, as Moses had foretold, gave them sacrifices.
WERE URGENT. Va-techezak (were urgent) is in the feminine, because the state of Egypt includes everything.
[WE ARE ALL DEAD.] I have explained its meaning in my comments on lest he fall upon us with pestilence (Ex. 5:3).

THEIR KNEADING-TROUGHS. Misheret (kneading-trough) is a wooden vessel. Compare, mishartekha (thy kneading-trough) in thy basket and thy kneading-trough (Deut. 28:5). Their asses were laden with garments which they asked of the Egyptians.

AND THE CHILDREN OF ISRAEL DID. Each one asked in accordance with his status. Thus we find that only the princes donated precious stones, spices, and oil for the work of the tabernacle (Ex. 35:27, 28).

AND THEY DESPOILED. We do not find the root nun, tzadi, lamed in the kal . We find it only in the hifil and the pi’el . They are both transitive verbs because there is no difference in meaning between va-yenatzelu (and they despoiled) and va-yatzel (hath taken away) in Thus God hath taken away (Gen. 31:9) except that in the hifil the object is mentioned and in the pi’el it is omitted.

AND THE CHILDREN OF ISRAEL JOURNEYED. The samekh in the word va-yisu (journeyed) should have received a dagesh to compensate for the missing nun , as the gimel in va-yiggeshu (and drew near) (Gen. 44:18) and the tav in va-yittenu (and they gave) (Gen. 35:4) do. It is possible that the dagesh was omitted to simplify enunciation.
FROM RAMESES. Rameses is vocalized with a pattach beneath the resh and a sheva beneath the ayin . It is not a city but rather the name of a district.
TO SUCCOTH. Sukkotah means: to Succoth.
[MEN.] Scripture mentions men. There was no need to mention the women because there were as many women as there were men, maybe even more.
BESIDE CHILDREN. Taf (children) refers to those under the age of twenty.
AND A MIXED MULTITUDE. Of Egyptians who intermingled with them. They are the asafsuf (mixed multitude) who joined them.
AND THEY BAKED. The dough which they brought out of Egypt had leaven in it. They did not bake it until they camped in Succoth.

NOW THE TIME THAT THE CHILDREN OF ISRAEL DWELT IN EGYPT WAS FOUR HUNDRED AND THIRTY YEARS. There are many calculations in Scripture whose point of departure is unknown to us. I will now mention a few of them. And it came to pass at the end of forty years, that Absalom said unto the king (II Sam. 15:7). Now Absalom was not then forty years old. Furthermore, King David’s reign was not yet over. The commentaries tell us that the point of departure for this calculation is from the day that the ark abode in Kiriath-jearim (I Sam. 7:2). It is stated, Now it came to pass in the thirtieth year (Ezek. 1:1). Some say that Ezekiel was thirty years old when he began to prophesy. Others say that the reference is to the thirtieth year of the jubilee. Other say that its point of departure is the finding of the Torah which was discovered by Hilkiah the priest. However, I am uncertain, for they are opinions without foundation or support. It is written: And within threescore and five years shall Ephraim be broken, that it be not a people (Is. 7:8). The latter prophesy was uttered during the days of Ahaz, whose reign lasted for sixteen years. Samaria was exiled in the sixth year of his son Hezekiah’s reign. The commentaries were therefore forced to say that the sixty-five years start from the day that Amos prophesied, And Israel shall surely be led away captive out of his land (Amos 7:11). Others say that its point of departure is the earthquake. Now when we investigated the years starting with the time that Israel came to Egypt in the days of Joseph and his brothers we found that they do not come to the number of years spoken of in Scripture. There is no doubt that Kehat was among those who descended to Egypt. Let us imagine that Kehat begot his son Amram at the end of his life and that Amram similarly begot Moses at the end of his life. Now the years of Kehat and Amram’s lives come to two hundred and seventy. Moses was eighty years old when the Israelites went out of Egypt. It all thus comes to three hundred and fifty years. We are missing eighty years. It is for this reason that the elders added, “dwelt in Egypt and other countries.” The four hundred years in and shall serve them; and they shall afflict them four hundred years (Gen. 15:13) is not connected to and they shall afflict them but rather to thy seed shall be a stranger ( Ibid. ). There are many other such instances. We similarly find in our own chapter, from the first day until the seventh day (v. 15). Now we find it stated that God told Abraham at the covenant made “between the pieces,” that thy seed shall be a stranger…four hundred years . We know that the number of years that Israel dwelt in Egypt is contingent upon the “end,” which was told to Abraham. The author of the Seder Olam was compelled to say that after Abraham came to the land of Canaan he returned to Haran. The commentaries were forced to say that the prophecy I am the Lord that brought thee out of Ur of the Chaldees (Gen. 15:7) is not connected to the above-noted chapter but was said later. However, there is no need for all of this. Only the counting of the four hundred years is from the day that Isaac was born. The additional thirty years start from the day that Abraham left Ur of the Chaldees, the land of his nativity, and came with his father to Haran, as it is written, and they came unto Haran, and dwelt there (Gen. 11: 31). Abraham lived in Haran with his father for five years. He came to the land of Canaan at the age of seventy-five and never returned to Haran. Now thirty years passed from the time that Abraham left Haran till the day Isaac was born. Abraham was the important one, and to him was the land of the Canaanite given. The verse I am the Lord that brought thee out of Ur of the Chaldees (Gen. 15:7) is connected to the entire chapter preceding and following it. The meaning of Now the time that the children of Israel dwelt in Egypt is to be explained: they were strangers there, also their fathers were strangers, as it is written, Yea, very few, and sojourners in it (Ps. 105:12); and as Abraham said, I am a stranger and a sojourner with you (Gen. 23:4).
FOUR HUNDRED AND THIRTY YEARS. From the day that their father Abraham left the land of his birth.

[AND IT CAME TO PASS AT THE END OF FOUR HUNDRED AND THIRTY YEARS.] Scripture states this so that it be known that they did not exit Egypt because of their cries to God until the time that the Lord had decreed for them had come.

IT WAS A NIGHT OF WATCHING UNTO THE LORD. Since Scripture notes, it was a night of watching unto the Lord , and concludes by saying, this same night is a night of watching unto the Lord for all the children of Israel throughout their generations , the plain meaning of our verse appears to be: since God watched them and did not suffer the destroyer to come into their homes to plague them, the Lord commanded that this night be a night of watching for all the children of Israel throughout their generations through the eating of the paschal lamb according to its ordinance and the ingesting of unleavened bread and bitter herbs on this night. Others say that watching here has the same meaning as the word watching in The watchers of the walls (Cant. 5:7); its meaning is that they should not sleep on this night but should praise God and relate the might that the Lord displayed when they went out of Egypt. Our sages hinted at the latter meaning when they said, The time for the reading of the morning shema has arrived .

AND THE LORD SAID…THIS IS THE ORDINANCE OF THE PASSOVER. Since Scripture mentioned t hat it was a night of watching (v. 42), the reference being to the night of the fifteenth wherein the paschal lamb is to be eaten, the Torah completes its explanation of the laws of the Passover that is to be observed in future generations. Now Scripture does not mention the lintel and the side-post. Neither does it mention that the lamb is to be eaten with unleavened bread and bitter herbs, as they were previously mentioned with regard to the Passover observed in Egypt. Its meaning thus is: you shall eat the Passover offering in the future as you ate it in Egypt. Scripture then added other commandments. However, the commandments with regard to the lintel and the side-post have nothing to do with the eating of the paschal lamb. Do you not see that at the beginning of the chapter (i.e., v. 43) it states, there shall no alien eat thereof (bo)? The meaning of bo (thereof) is, of it. Its usage in this context is correct in Hebrew and also in Arabic. Ve-hanotar ba-basar u-va-lechem (and that which remaineth of the flesh and of the bread) (Lev. 8:32) is similar.

BUT EVERY MAN’S SERVANT…WHEN THOU HAST CIRCUMCISED HIM. According to his wish, that he be converted to the law of Israel, if he is of the age when one is obligated to observe the commandments. The law dealing with someone that is bought for money and someone born in the house is the same. However, Scripture deals with that which is more prevalent.
A SOJOURNER AND A HIRED SERVANT. Who are Israelites shall not eat of the paschal lamb if a portion of the lamb has not been assigned to them, as is the law for the entire congregation.

IN ONE HOUSE SHALL IT BE EATEN. As the paschal lamb eaten in Egypt was. Thou shalt not carry forth aught of the flesh abroad out of the house is proof of this. However, our sages of blessed memory said that in one house means in one company. The latter is the correct interpretation.

ALL THE CONGREGATION OF ISRAEL SHALL KEEP IT. All those of the age when one is obligated to observe the commandments are required to prepare a paschal lamb. When I researched the Torah, I found that the twenty-three times where karet (excision) is stated refer to negative precepts. However, I found only two dealing with positive precepts, namely, the paschal lamb and circumcision. Perhaps the reason for this is that there is an obligation to “remember” the Exodus from Egypt, and there is no greater manifestation of “remembering” than eating the paschal lamb in its proper time. And the beginning of the decalogue states, I am the Lord thy God, who brought thee out of the land of Egypt (Ex. 20:2).
AND WHEN A STRANGER SHALL SOJOURN WITH THEE. The meaning of with thee is, with thee in the land of Egypt.
[AND WILL KEEP THE PASSOVER.] Its meaning is, and he wants to keep the Passover. Then let him first be circumcised.
[BUT NO UNCIRCUMCISED PERSON SHALL EAT THERE-OF.] The reference is to uncircumcised Israelites such as those born on the way in the wilderness.
ONE LAW. The stranger spoken of in this verse refers to a righteous proselyte, not to a stranger that dwells within the gates.

[THUS DID ALL THE CHILDREN OF ISRAEL.] Scripture has already mentioned this above. Perhaps the reason it is noted again is that it refers to the Passover offering brought in the wilderness of Sinai, at which time the strangers were circumcised. Do not be surprised that this is written in this place. Scripture states in the chapter dealing with the coming down of the manna that they should take a jar and put manna therein and place it before the Lord (Ex. 16:33). However, God had not yet commanded the making of the ark of the testimony. Have I brought your hosts out of the land of Egypt (v. 17) is similar.

AND IT CAME TO PASS THE SELFSAME DAY. I believe that this verse is connected to the verse which follows, in which God told Moses to sanctify the first-born. The plague of the first-born took place at midnight, and when Israel went out of Egypt the next day God immediately commanded that the first-born of Israel and the first-born of their cattle be sanctified.

AND THE LORD SPOKE. Scripture employs a short form, for Moses stands in place of Israel. However, Yefet says that Moses was commanded to verbally sanctify all first-born. The aforementioned is the reverse of then the priest shall defile him (Lev. 13:8); the priest, being holy, defiles an individual by declaration.

OPENETH. Peter (openeth) means the opening of. Peter is similar to peture (open) in and open flowers (I Kings 6:18). Its meaning is, the son who first opens the womb. The word rechem (womb) is irregular, as according to the rules of Hebrew grammar the letter preceding a guttural is vocalized with a pattach .
AND MOSES SAID. Remember this day was said by Moses on the fifteenth day. It means the same as And this day shall be unto you for a memorial (Ex. 12:14).

[OUT OF THE HOUSE OF BONDAGE.] This indicates that the Egyptians forced them to work as if they were their slaves. Elsewhere Scripture reads, out of the iron furnace (Deut. 4:20), for the Egyptians overpowered them. However, the Lord brought them out by strength of hand from the mighty.

THIS DAY. Moses first mentions, there shall be no leavened bread eaten , its meaning being, do in future generations what you did on the day that you left Egypt. As you left Egypt at the time when the first ears ( aviv ) are found, so shall you do yearly in the future in the Land of Israel when the first ears come. The first ears refers to the first ears of barley. The word aviv (Abib) means the first that ripens. Aviv comes from the same root as av (father), which means first to the one whom one begets, or sage to the student whom one teaches. Furthermore, it is written, for the barley was in the ear (aviv) (Ex. 9:31). Even of the first-fruits (bikkure) of wheat harvest (Ex. 34:22), which is written with regard to the festival of weeks, is proof of the above.
AND IT SHALL BE. Scripture does not list all of the seven Canaanite nations because they have already been mentioned elsewhere.
THE SEVEN DAYS. This is the service.

UNLEAVENED BREAD. Now the stranger that is within the gate was exhorted by God to observe the Sabbath, as it is only on the condition that he do no work before the Lord on the Sabbath that he may dwell within the gates. Similarly on the Day of Atonement, for it is so written. The same applies to Passover, as a stranger is not permitted to eat leaven even on his own property. This is the meaning of in all thy borders .

IT IS BECAUSE OF THAT. Rabbi Merinus says that ba’avur zeh (it is because of that) should have been written, zeh ba’avur ; i.e., this is because of what the Lord did for me. He cited what in his opinion are many other such instances. However, I do not think that he was right in even one instance. For how can we invert the words of the living God? The meaning of the verse is just the opposite of what he understands it to be, because we do not eat unleavened bread “because of this.” Its meaning rather is: it is because of this, i.e., it is because of this service, namely, the eating of unleavened bread and the abstention from leavened bread, which are the first of the precepts that God commanded us, that the Lord did signs for us and brought us out of Egypt. Its meaning thus is: God took us out of Egypt only to serve Him, as it is written, when thou hast brought forth the people out of Egypt, ye shall serve God upon this mountain (Ex. 20:12). It is furthermore stated, I am the Lord your God, who brought you out of the land of Egypt, to be your God : I am the Lord your God (Num. 15:41).

AND IT SHALL BE A SIGN UNTO THEE. There are those who oppose our holy patriarchs and say that for a sign…and for a memorial is to be understood in the manner of For they shall be a chaplet of grace unto thy head, And chains about thy head (Prov. 1:9). They also say that And thou shalt bind them for a sign upon thy hand (Deut. 5:8) is like Bind them continually upon thy heart, Tie them upon thy neck (Prov. 6:21) and also that And thou shalt write them upon the door-posts of thy house (Deut. 6:9) is like Write them upon the table of thy heart (Prov. 3:3). They furthermore say that it shall be for a sign…and for a memorial means for with a strong hand hath the Lord brought thee out of Egypt shall drop from your lips. However, this is incorrect, for at the beginning of the book of Proverbs it is stated, The Proverbs of Solomon . Thus whatever Solomon henceforth mentions is by way of parable. However, it is not, heaven forbid, written in the Torah that it is metaphoric. Hence it is to be taken only at face value. We thus will not interpret it except literally. It does not contradict reason if explained according to its plain meaning, like Circumcise therefore the foreskin of your heart (Deut. 10:16), which has to be interpreted according to the requirements of reason.

[UPON THY HAND.] Rabbi Moses Ha-Kohen says that the term yad (hand) in most of Scripture refers to the left hand, as in Yea, My hand (yadi) hath laid the foundation of the earth, And My right hand hath spread out the heavens (Is. 48:13); and Her hand (yadah) she put to the tent-pin, And her right hand to the workmen’s hammer (Jud. 5:26). However, the teachings of tradition are firmly established and do not require any support.

FROM YEAR TO YEAR. Mi-yamim yamimah (from year to year) is similar to yamim tiheyeh ge’ullato (for a full year shall he have the right of redemption (Lev. 25:29). The meaning of mi-yamim yamimah is, from year to year. The year begins when the Bet Din announces its commencement.
AND IT SHALL BE. Moses mentions only the Canaanite, because he was the father of them all.
[AS HE SWORE UNTO THEE.] Its meaning is similar to for unto thee, and unto thy seed, I will give this land (Gen. 26:3).
THAT THOU SHALT SET APART. Thou shalt set it apart unto the Lord so that it does not get mixed up with another. Now these two precepts were commanded on the fifteenth day.

COMING OF. Sheger (coming of) follows the paradigm of eretz (land of) whose vocalization does not change in the construct. However, a number of irregular cases are found. They are: shegar (the increase of) in the increase of thy kine (Deut. 7:13), chadar (chamber of) in and in the chamber of thy bed (Ex. 7:28), havel (vanity of) in Vanity of vanities (Eccles. 1:1), hamatekha (thy venom) in That puttest thy venom thereto (Hab. 2:15), and delatekha (thy doors) in and shut the doors (Is. 26:20). I have not found any additional instances.
AND EVERY FIRSTLING OF AN ASS. Which is unclean, thou shalt redeem with a lamb .

THOU SHALT BREAK ITS NECK. Some say that va-arafto (thou shalt break its neck) means thou shalt write the word holy on its neck. However, I say that anyone who says this is himself a stiff-necked ass. For behold it is written, He will break down (ya’arof) their altars (Hos. 10:2), and ve-arefu sham et ha-eglah ba-nachal (and shall break the heifer’s neck there in the valley) (Deut. 21:4), in which the meaning of ve-arefu is, as explained by the transmitters of the law, to cut off the neck. All firstlings that are not brought up on the altar or are not redeemed are required to be killed, as all the first-born of Egypt both man and beast perished. God did not save them from the decree which he had issued on the first-born of the Egyptians except that they should be prepared for His service. The Israelites had no unclean animals except for asses. Therefore no other first-born is to be redeemed.
AND IT SHALL BE. Rabbi Judah Ha-Levi of blessed memory says that the word machar (in time to come) is missing an alef , its meaning being that which comes after today.

AND IT CAME TO PASS. Moses begins by saying, By strength of hand the Lord brought us out from Egypt (v. 14) and backtracks and explains that what the strength of hand refers to is the plague of the first-born. It was because of this plague, and not because of the first plagues, that Israel went out of Egypt. The poet similarly says, To Him that smote Egypt in their first-born, For His mercy endureth for ever (Ps. 136:10). Moses wrote elliptically. When Moses said, that the Lord slew all the first-born in the land of Egypt, both the first-born of man, and the first-born of beasts , it was known that God saved our first-born and the first-born of our cattle. It is to the latter, not to the slaying of the first-born, that therefore I sacrifice to the Lord all that openeth the womb is connected.
ALL THAT OPENETH THE WOMB, BEING MALES. From a kind fit to be sacrificed to the Lord.

AND IT SHALL BE FOR A SIGN. Scripture mentions, And it shall be for a sign upon thy hand with regard to two commandments. That which the sages of blessed memory transmitted, namely, that the chapters are to be written, is true.

AND FOR FRONTLETS. Totafot (frontlets) means a memorial. Others say that the tet of totafot is doubled, its meaning being to speak. They say that it comes from the same root as ve-hettef (and preach) in and preach toward the south (Ezek. 21:2). However, in my opinion this is far-fetched.
Can a fool who rebels against his maker succeed? When at peace his liver an arrow shall split. Note and take heed, O recusant; All that the portion Be-Shallach records concerning Pharaoh.

AND IT CAME TO PASS WHEN PHARAOH HAD LET THE PEOPLE GO. The vav in ve-lo nacham (led them not) is like an unaspirated fa in the Arabic tongue. It is known that the distance between Egypt and Jerusalem by way of the land of the Philistines is not very great. It is about a ten-day journey by straight road. If this was not so, how did the tribes come as far as Egypt upon their asses? If the distance was very great how much would have been necessary for them and their asses to eat? Furthermore, upon returning they brought back food for their households.

ALTHOUGH THAT WAS NEAR. Rabbi Moses Ha-Kohen says that ki karov hu means although that was near . In my opinion, ki am keshe oref hu (for it is a stiff-necked people) (Ex. 34:9); refa’ah nafshi ki chatati lakh (Heal my soul; for I have sinned against Thee) (Ps. 41:5); and ki rekhev barzel lo (though they have chariots of iron) (Josh. 17:18) are similar. However, I see no need for this interpretation, for its meaning is: the reason God did not lead them by way of the land of the Philistines was that it was close. God thus led them via a distant way so that they would not witness any war and say, Let us make a captain, and let us return to Egypt (Num. 14:4).

[LEST PERADVENTURE.] We know for certain that the Lord knows the future. God knew that the people would repent if He led them by the way of the land of the Philistines. Scripture reads, Lest peradventure the people repent because the Torah employed human terminology so that those who study will understand.

LED THE PEOPLE ABOUT. Va-yassev (led about) is a verb that comes from a double root. Its stem is samekh, bet, bet. Va-yassev also has an alternative vocalization. Compare, va-yasekh (shut up) in Or who shut up (Job 38:8) and va-yagel (and rolled) in and rolled the stone (Gen. 29:10). Pay no heed to those who say that the root of va- yassev is nun, samekh, bet .

[THE WILDERNESS.] The word ha-midbar (the wilderness) is to be read as if written twice. The clause is to be understood as if written, by the way of the wilderness, wilderness of the Red Sea. Similarly, ha-aron ha-bebrit (the ark of the covenant) (Josh. 3:14) is to be understood as if written, the ark, ark of the covenant, and, ve-etz ha-da’at tov va-ra (the tree of the knowledge of good and evil) (Gen. 2:9) as if written, and the tree of the knowledge, knowledge of good and evil. Likewise the terms ha-sefer ha-miknah (the deed of the purchase) (Jer. 32:12) and ha-yayin ha-chemah (the wine of fury) (Jer. 25:15). There are many other similar instances.

RED SEA. Suf (Red) is the name of a place. Others say that suf comes from the same root as sof (the end) in The end of the matter (Eccles. 12:13). It is so called because it lies at the end of the world. The reference is to the Atlantic, which I have already mentioned. However, this is a major blunder, because the yam suf (Red Sea) lies in the east, opposite Egypt. The Spanish Sea is larger than it.

ARMED. Some say that chamushim (armed) means full of wealth, possessing all that they need. Now Scripture states, neither had they prepared for themselves any victual (Ex. 12:39). Furthermore, what reason is there to mention this now? The only meaning of chamushim is, girded with weapons for war. Compare, chalutzim ta’avoru (ye shall pass over armed) (Deut. 3:18), the meaning of which is: ye shall pass over with girded loins. The fact that Scripture in one place reads, ve-attem ta’averu chamushim (but ye shall pass over before your brethren armed) (Josh. 1:14) and in another place refers to the Israelites as chalutzim (Deut. 3:18) is true witness to the aforementioned. What reason was there for them to carry food before their brethren? The reason Scripture at this point notes that the children of Israel went up armed is that it is previously stated, Lest peradventure the people repent when they see war, and they return to Egypt (v. 17). For the Israelites went out with a high hand (Ex. 14:8), with weapons of war and not like fleeing slaves.

AND MOSES TOOK THE BONES OF JOSEPH. Scripture mentions above that the children of Israel who were alive in that generation went up out of the land of Egypt . Scripture now notes that the children of Israel also brought up with them the most honored one of them, the one through whom they came down to Egypt. The latter had made them swear before his death that they would tell their children, and their children would instruct their children about this. Now Moses busied himself with fulfilling the oath so that no guilt would fall upon Israel. For we see that the princes of Israel swore an oath to the Gibeonites. Now they only took this oath on condition that the Gibeonites came from a distant place as they claimed. After it was found that the Gibeonites came from close by it was fitting that they not keep their oath so that they and all Israel not violate the injunction, thou shalt save alive nothing (Deut. 20:16). However, they kept their oath out of regard for God’s glory so that they not desecrate it. Many years later God punished the children of Israel because Saul permitted the Gibeonites who were in Nob, the city of the priests, to be put to death.
[THE BONES OF JOSEPH.] Scripture mentions the bones of for all of the flesh and skin breeds worms and putrefies, and after a few years only the bones remain.
AND THEY TOOK THEIR JOURNEY…ETHAM. Etham is, as I will explain, the wilderness of Shur.

AND THE LORD WENT BEFORE THEM BY DAY. We know that the Lord inhabiteth eternity and His name is Holy (Is. 57:15), and that He is enthroned of old. Selah (Ps. 55:20). Scripture speaks in the language of men. It reads so because God’s power went with Israel, as in That caused His glorious arm to go at the right hand of Moses (Is. 63:12).

[IN A PILLAR OF CLOUD.] Scripture reads, in a pillar of cloud because it was not shaped like other clouds but was in the form of a pillar stretching from the sky upon the earth. A pillar is called an ammud in Hebrew because the base ( ma’amad ) of the house is on it.

[THAT THEY MIGHT GO BY DAY AND BY NIGHT.] Scripture reads, that they might go by day and by night because the camp was large and they could only journey a short distance. They therefore journeyed part of the day and also part of the night. These two pillars were, as I shall explain, before the Israelites until they came to the sea.
DEPARTED NOT. Yamish (departed) is a transitive verb. For God mentioned above did not cause the pillars to depart from before the people.

[BY DAY.] The word yomam (by day) is not found employed in Scripture except for the time when the sun shines upon the earth. The word yom (day) found in the Torah, the Prophets, and the Writings refers also to nighttime, for it is written, on the day (yom) that I smote all the first-born in the land of Egypt (Num. 8:17). Now the slaying of the first-born took place at night. It is also written, this day (ha-yom) is a day (yom) of good tidings (II Kings 7:9). Now it was then night, for we read there, if we tarry till the morning light ( Ibid. ). Scripture also reads, The day (yom) I cry in the night before Thee (Ps. 88:2).
